taskDescription: Arrange the steps of enteric fever pathogenesis in the correct chronological order.
paragraphs: Salmonella Typhi is ingested in contaminated food or water (infective dose 10⁵–10⁷ organisms)
Organisms cross the intestinal epithelium via M-cells overlying Peyer's patches in the terminal ileum
Salmonella survives within macrophages by suppressing phagosome-lysosome fusion using Salmonella Pathogenicity Islands
Primary bacteraemia develops as organisms travel from mesenteric lymph nodes into the bloodstream (end of incubation period)
Systemic seeding of liver, spleen, gallbladder, and bone marrow occurs during secondary multiplication
Secondary bacteraemia produces the clinical syndrome with step-ladder fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and risk of intestinal perforation
